roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a divisional clash in Week 6. He rushed 24 times for 102 yards and caught one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. The game marked Henry's first scoreless outing on the ground in 2026, and he draws a difficult Week 6 matchup against a Browns' defense that has surrendered just one combined TD to the position. Cleveland ranks seventh by allowing 17.6 fantasy points per game to RBs, but the Jets' Braelon Allen racked up 116 rushing yards and one score on 24 attempts in Week 5. The Browns could again be without two starters on the defensive line, and with Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status in question, Henry has another opportunity to be the primary engine of the offense.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to do more as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Loveland wasn't able to build on a solid six catches for 57 yards in Week 4, reeling in just two of five targets for 19 yards versus the Packers in Week 5. The second-year pass catcher has been thrown to by three quarterbacks of varying skill so far this year, which could add to the struggles of his output. He'll take on an Atalnta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson commands a heavy volume of targets in the Jets' passing game heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Wilson collected 11 looks in Week 5, topping 100 yards for the second time this season, and has now garnered at least seven targets in four of five outings. New England's secondary is banged up, and the availability of star CB Christian Gonzalez remains uncertain. While the Jets don't want to pass heavily, when they do, targets should be funneled toward Wilson. He has a great chance to exploit a defense that has allowed two 100-yard receivers this season.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore continues to battle through a shoulder issue that's cost him the better part of three games as the Bills head towards a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Moore has drawn 18 targets in his two healthy games, making his shoulder the only factor to worry about when considering him in lineups. The Raiders have allowed at least 91 yards to an opposing wideout in three straight weeks, adding confidence to Moore's viability if he proves healthy.

roster.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
roster.outlook: Marvin Harrison could make his Texans debut in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Harrison will likely be brought along slowly after being acquired in a trade from Arizona, so expectations should be tempered for Week 6, though the 2024 fourth overall pick is at least worth a flier in deeper leagues against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers. Harrison had just 85 receiving yards in four games for the Cardinals this season, but a reunion with former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud could be what Harrison needs to get his career back on track. While catching passes from Stroud in 2022, Harrison posted his best college season, with 77 catches for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.

roster.name: Kenyon Sadiq
roster.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq will need to clear the league's concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. After a breakout Week 3 performance, Sadiq has just two catches for three yards (seven targets) over the last two games. New England struggled against Brock Bowers in Week 5 but had previously not allowed more than 32 yards or a touchdown to opposing tight ends. With Geno Smith not throwing a plethora of passes, Sadiq has minimal fantasy allure. Mason Taylor would elevate if Sadiq sits.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence threw for a season-high 331 yards against the Eagles as the Jaguars improved to 4-1 with a Week 5 win. He brings a 10:3 TD:INT into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans, which will be the Jaguars' second consecutive game in London. Houston has surprisingly been one of the league's most generous pass defenses, allowing QBs to throw for 256 yards per game, though the Texans have allowed only six TDs through the air. Lawrence produced just 380 passing yards with a 1:2 TD:INT in two meetings with the AFC South rival Texans in 2025, but since Houston's defense has taken a step back this season, Lawrence can continue to be deployed as a starting fantasy QB for Week 6.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro enters a Week 6 tilt against Washington coming off hitting a game-winning field goal for San Francisco this past Sunday. The veteran kicker missed a 52-yard attempt in that contest, but he atoned for that with a 44-yard make that ended up being the deciding score. Pineiro is now 5-for-8 on FG attempts this season, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. He could see plenty of chances against the Commanders, who are allowing the third-most points (29.8) in the league.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen's role for the Jets in Week 6 against the Patriots is in flux due to uncertainty surrounding Breece Hall (quad). Allen has dominated carries in two games with Hall out, breaking out in Week 5 with a 24-carry, 116-yard performance. New England hasn't allowed an opposing back to gain over 75 yards, and Allen hasn't been a factor in the Jets' passing game. If Hall does not return, volume will be Allen's best asset.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He hauled in six of nine targets for 80 yards and had one carry for four yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 Week 5 victory. With Roman Wilson (finger) injured in the win and already ruled out for the meeting with the Buccaneers, Bernard has a real opportunity to fill that void and continue contributing in his debut season. The 2026 second-round pick notched career highs but is still searching for his first career touchdown, something he hopes to change against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua is coming off a massive performance on Monday Night Football with the Rams' Week 6 clash against the Cardinals on tap. Nacua recorded career-best marks with 17 catches and 24 targets in Week 5 against Buffalo, turning that enormous volume into 138 yards and a touchdown while adding nine yards on two carries. The TD was Nacua's first over three games this season, but he's otherwise been massively productive in averaging 10.3 receptions and 112.3 receiving yards per game. The Cardinals don't figure to offer much resistance, as they've yielded the second-most fantasy points per game (28.0) to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers continues to make up for lost time, producing an 8-110-1 line on 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After missing the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from knee surgery, the superstar tight end has gotten into the end zone in three straight weeks, amassing 24 catches for 312 yards and three scores on 35 targets. Bowers is the clear top option for Kirk Cousins in the passing game, and that isn't likely to change even if Las Vegas eventually switches to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. Bowers will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers saw a staggering 20 targets last game for the Giants. Nabers parlayed those ample opportunities into 11 grabs for 121 yards and a touchdown. It was the second-straight 100-yard outing for Nabers, who also scored for the second-consecutive contest. His newfound connection with starting quarterback Jameis Winston has been evident. In Week 6, the G-Men face a New Orleans defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Saints are allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate crashed back down to earth in Week 5, producing just one catch for six yards against the Texans while playing through a back injury after breaking out for a career-high 145 receiving yards against the Eagles in Week 4. Tennessee's fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will likely remain a boom-or-bust fantasy option throughout his rookie campaign while occupying a starting role in what has been the worst offense in the league. A Week 6 road game against the Colts appears more likely to deliver a peak than a valley, assuming Tate is close to full health, as Indianapolis is giving up 160 receiving yards per game and 15 yards per catch to wideouts. Tate is a high-ceiling Week 6 flex option.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will aim to return to the field as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Monangai sat out in Week 5 with a toe injury, but he's week-to-week and not a candidate for IR. The second-year ball carrier put together a career-best 30 rushes for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets in Week 4, so he could be inching towards a featured role if he can get back to the field. If he plays, Monangai will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, while also producing season highs in touches (20) and rushing yards (68). The veteran running back was one of the few players to clearly benefit from Sean Payton's return to play-calling duties, but Dobbins still managed fairly modest numbers. He's been able to stay healthy so far in 2026, but through five games he's averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, a mark that would be a career low if it doesn't improve. Dobbins will take on a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that's tied for 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but which has yet to allow any back to reach 70 rushing yards in a game.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.outlook: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.

roster.name: Tyler Loop
roster.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.

roster.name: Kalif Raymond
roster.outlook: Kalif Raymond will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has now caught five passes for just 12 yards in the past two weeks. Chicago has had struggles at the quarterback position in this stretch, but the veteran still appears behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR pecking order. Raymond will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to his position this season.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey has had a nose for the end zone this season and will look to score again when the 49ers face the Commanders in Week 6. McCaffrey produced 83 total yards and a TD this past Sunday in a big win over Seattle, giving him at least one score four straight weeks. While his 16.0 touches per game this year are considerably lower than his 24.3 last season, he's been more efficient on the ground with 4.7 yards per carry (he averaged just 3.9 YPC during the regular season in 2025). With that said, Washington has been stingy against RBs through five weeks, yielding just 3.76 YPC and only two total touchdowns.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall needs to overcome a quad injury to suit up for the first time in three weeks when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Braelon Allen has shouldered the load in Hall's absence, and a split workload can be anticipated once Hall returns. Hall would require an unlikely heavy volume to be a top option facing a New England defense that's allowed just 399 rushing yards through five games.

roster.name: Davante Adams
roster.outlook: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns are back home to host the Ravens for an AFC North divisional tilt in Week 6. It was a quiet day for the sophomore tight end, as he caught just one of four targets for four yards during Cleveland's 17-12 defeat in Week 5. Fannin notched at least 50 receiving yards or caught a touchdown in three straight outings prior to this dud, so fantasy managers can blame the poor showing on weather. He'll look to get back into the end zone versus a Baltimore defense that surrendered five receptions for 42 yards and a TD to Kyle Pitts Sr. in their last outing.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday. Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.

roster.name: Kaelon Black
roster.outlook: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker has hauled in at least four passes in four straight games as the Raiders' top wide receiver, although he plays a clear second fiddle to tight end Brock Bowers in the passing game. Tucker has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in three of those games, and his only touchdown came during his Week 2 eruption against the Chargers. The fourth-year wideout will have a ceiling game once in a blue moon, but his weekly floor is low, at least while Kirk Cousins remains under center instead of rookie Fernando Mendoza. Tucker will try to get enough volume to take advantage of a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Sam Darnold
roster.outlook: Sam Darnold will look to bounce back from a rough performance when Seattle visits Denver in Week 6. Darnold was picked off twice this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, and he threw for a modest 195 yards with one touchdown. He now has an uninspiring 7:5 TD:INT through four games after recording the third-most pickoffs (14) among NFL quarterbacks during the regular season last year. The Broncos don't figure to offer much relief, as they've yielded the fifth-best passer rating (79.4) this season.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Dameon Pierce
roster.outlook: Dameon Pierce was the last running back standing for the Eagles last game. Will Shipley started the game and found the end zone early for the Eagles, but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. Pierce could start against the Panthers, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is arguably the most matchup-proof wideout in the NFL, but he could be challenged in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Smith-Njigba caught five of eight targets for 102 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco in a loss this past Sunday. He's now recorded at least 100 receiving yards and one touchdown in four of his five games this season, and Smith-Njigba leads the league with 583 receiving yards. He'll be matched up Week 6 against a Broncos defense that has allowed the third-lowest catch rate (54.5%) to wideouts, but Smith-Njigba figures to get a big boost by not having to face star cornerback Patrick Surtain, who is expected to miss the contest due to an ankle injury.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to remain the focal point of Tampa Bay's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Irving was phenomenal in the Week 5 upset win over the Cowboys, totaling 175 yards and two touchdowns on 23 touches. Despite this, Irving is seeing less receiving work since Jalon Daniels took over for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback, getting just three targets over his last two games. Even so, Irving should remain productive in Week 6 against a Steelers defense that's allowed 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton ended his touchdown drought in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, catching two of three targets for 18 yards and his first score of the season. The team's entire offense has been sluggish to begin the year, and having Sean Payton take over play-calling duties didn't pay immediate dividends, but it should bode well for Sutton in the long run. He'll face another tough challenge in Week 6 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce remains on pace for a bounce-back season coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. Through four games, the veteran tight end is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022, although it's fair to wonder if he can keep that up given his reduced volume, as he's also on track to fall short of 100 targets for the first time since 2014. With Kenneth Walker having rejuvenated the team's rushing game and Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy both capable of handling underneath and intermediate routes, there isn't a clear niche for Kelce to thrive in. He remains Patrick Mahomes' most trustworthy option, and that should keep his floor relatively high. Kelce will take on a Chargers defense in Week 6 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.outlook: Tyler Shough is expected to remain productive in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Shough had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, completing just 16 of 25 pass attempts for 96 yards and two interceptions. Despite this, he currently ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards (1,299) through five games, attempting a league-leading 205 pass attempts. He could definitely bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 22.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Cairo Santos
roster.outlook: Cairo Santos will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Santos missed his only field-goal attempt and converted an XPA in a Week 6 blowout loss to the Packers. The veteran kicker has now converted seven of nine field-goal kicks and all 14 of his extra-point tries across five games this season. He'll face an Atlanta squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers this campaign.

roster.name: MarShawn Lloyd
roster.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be Green Bay's primary option in the running game again versus the Cowboys in Week 6. Lloyd put together his best fantasy performance of the year versus the Bears in Week 5, recording 10 carries for 31 yards and two touchdowns along with one catch for six yards. The second-year ball carrier has totaled 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 40 carries and caught 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score across the first five games of the campaign. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Pat Freiermuth
roster.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 6. He played 38 snaps on offense (70%) and was highly productive, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two of Aaron Rodgers' three TD passes during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Freiermuth finished third on the team in receptions and yardage, while his seven looks were the second-most. Fellow starting tight end Darnell Washington was on the field for 34 offensive snaps (63%) and caught two of three targets for 12 yards. Freiermuth recorded a second consecutive outing with a score and now has four TDs on the season, and he'll aim to take advantage of a Tampa Bay defense allowing 15.7 fantasy points per game (22nd) to TEs.

roster.name: Makai Lemon
roster.outlook: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Dominic Zvada
roster.outlook: Dominic Zvada had an afternoon to forget last game for the Giants. The rookie missed three kicks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. Coming into the game, Zvada had not missed a single boot. However, he subsequently missed three field goals from 40-plus yards out. While the conditions were rather poor and the missed attempts were long, Zvada did also hit two other  tries from 50-plus yards away, as well as all three of his extra points. Despite the rough outing, Zvada should remain the kicker in Week 6 versus the Saints. New Orleans is allowing 30.2 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league, so Zvada should get plenty of chances for redemption.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top receiving option in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. McMillan is coming off the best performance of his young career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, recording career highs in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (192) while scoring two touchdowns. He ranks ninth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.3) through four appearances this season, leading Carolina in yards, targets and receptions. Expect McMillan to remain productive in Week 6 against an Eagles secondary that's allowed 38.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze remains a top option in Chicago's passing game ahead of Week 6 at Atlanta. Odunze brought in just three of his nine targets for 40 yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers, but he still ranked second in receiving yards. The volatility of the Bears' quarterback position has affected Odunze's production so far this season, so the return of Caleb Williams would likely be favorable. Either way, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. The two-time league MVP sat out Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5 with a sprained left ankle. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed Monday that Jackson is "definitely doing better" in his recovery, but there's still no guarantee that he'll be ready for the trip to Cleveland. Tyler Huntley filled in admirably as the starting QB, throwing for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score in the OT victory. Jackson will need to practice in some form before the Ravens can determine his status against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to the position.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Thomas is coming off a Week 5 goose egg against the Eagles and has just 25 receiving yards over Jacksonville's last three games after kicking off the season with consecutive 40-yard performances. The 2024 first-round pick has a snap share below 50% this season heading into a Week 6 matchup against the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to defend WRs, allowing 193 yards per game to the position, but Thomas isn't a trustworthy fantasy option despite the favorable matchup given his recent struggles. Unless you are desperate for a bye-week plug-in in a deeper format, Thomas should be left on the bench if not dropped outright.

roster.name: Jake Ferguson
roster.outlook: Jake Ferguson saw a season-high six targets last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which likely contributed to the additional looks for other players, including Ferguson. However, Ferguson managed three catches for just 19 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Ferguson back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught four of six targets for 28 yards and lost a fumble during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Andrews is averaging a solid six targets through five outings in 2026, but he's yet to top 50 receiving yards, only has one touchdown, and tallies 35.4 yards per contest. He'll look to break out versus a Browns defense that's tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to TEs.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Young has performed very well to start the season, leading the NFL in passing yards per game (317) while accounting for 10 total touchdowns. In his most recent performance, a Week 4 win over the Lions, Young threw for a whopping 329 yards and two touchdowns. He's expected to remain one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while facing an Eagles defense that's allowed 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

roster.name: Kenny Gainwell
roster.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to remain the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Gainwell has operated as Tampa Bay's top receiving back over the last two weeks, getting more targets (six), receptions (five) and yards (32) than Bucky Irving (two catches on three targets for 10 yards). Despite this, Gainwell will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without scoring a touchdown. He could thrive against a Pittsburgh defense that's allowed 200 receiving yards to RBs through five contests, tied for the third-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Andy Borregales
roster.outlook: Andy Borregales will look to remain busy when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. With New England's offense coming to life over the last two weeks, Borregales has nailed nine PATs over that span, but their efficiency has yielded only one field goal. The Jets have allowed nine field goals and nine PATs through five games, ranking in the middle, and if those averages hold, Borregales can be an adequate streamer.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has three multi-TD outings on the ground through five games, and he's likely to be the focal point of the Colts' offense in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who are surrendering 120 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Taylor averages 23 touches per game and should handle a heavy workload, with the Colts expected to play from ahead at home. Start the star RB, who is averaging 101 scrimmage yards per game, with confidence in this clash between AFC South rivals.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride will look to remain productive for Arizona's offense in Week 6 against the Rams. McBride put up another big line against Detroit this past Sunday, catching nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end leads all NFL players with 42 receptions this season, and only Amon-Ra St. Brown (57) has more targets than McBride's 56. That should mean McBride gets plenty of opportunities against the Rams, but to find success he'll have to overcome a defense that is giving up the fewest fantasy points per game (3.2) to tight ends this season.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten remains Jacksonville's starting RB heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans. He has recorded at least 88 scrimmage yards in four of five games while occupying that role and has two rushing TDs this season. Houston has been among the league's stingiest defenses against RBs, limiting the position to 89 scrimmage yards per game and allowing only three TDs on 103 carries. Tuten's prominent role in an above-average offense keeps him in the fantasy RB2 range despite the tricky Week 6 matchup.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.outlook: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington bounced back from a seven-yard Week 4 dud with his best game of the season in Week 5, racking up 124 yards and two TDs against the Eagles. Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver is averaging 70 yards per game and has four TDs through five outings while leading the Jaguars in every receiving category. Washington can be penciled in as a fantasy WR1 for Week 6 against a Texans pass defense that has been surprisingly weak, allowing 193 receiving yards per game to wideouts and six TDs in five games to the position, making it one of the five most generous defenses against wideouts.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey did not have much work last game for Dallas. Aubrey connected on one field goal and one extra point in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Aubrey has made just nine field goals through five games for Dallas, which is tied for 10th in the league. In Week 6, the Cowboys face the Packers. Green Bay is allowing 22.4 points per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.outlook: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to return for the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Coker was on a tear to start the season, catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina's first two games. He's expected to continue benefitting from the new, aggressive Panthers offense, led by Bryce Young, who's averaging 40.5 passing attempts per game this year. Coker will likely find success if active in Week 6 against an Eagles defense that's given up seven touchdowns to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Johnson tallied just 16 yards on four receptions in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, struggling alongside the rest of New Orleans' offense. Despite this, he's tied for the second-most receptions (25) on the Saints through five weeks, accumulating 248 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Johnson to bounce back in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's allowed 14.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this year.

roster.name: Emanuel Wilson
roster.outlook: Emanuel Wilson will look to get into the end zone for a third straight game when the Seahawks travel to Denver in Week 6. Wilson has emerged as Seattle's clear top RB over the past two weeks, registering 41 carries for 142 yards and two touchdowns on the ground along with five catches for 50 yards and another score through the air in that span. He figures to continue working as the team's No. 1 RB at least until one or both of Zach Charbonnet (knee) or Jadarian Price (chest) is able to return, but that won't happen in Week 6. The Broncos have been vulnerable against the run this season, surrendering 4.51 yards per carry to running backs (eighth-worst in the league).

roster.name: Dontayvion Wicks
roster.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks led all Eagles wideouts in targets last game. Wicks was targeted eight times en route to five catches for 63 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Wicks, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

roster.name: Seth McGowan
roster.outlook: Seth McGowan has 20 touches for 71 yards through five NFL games with the Colts. The rookie seventh-round pick is a distant second on Indianapolis' RB depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. There is a greater chance than usual of the Colts pulling away and resting Taylor in a Week 6 home game against the 0-5 Titans, but banking on a lopsided game is an unreliable strategy, so McGowan is best left out of fantasy lineups in Week 6.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb is said to be dealing with a bruise of his quadriceps, but he is not expected to miss any time for the Cowboys. Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards last game as he was dealing with the issue. That snapped a three-game streak for Lamb of at least 112 yards receiving. He will look to get back on track in Week 6 versus the Packers. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker was dominant for Kansas City in the team's first four games prior to a Week 5 bye, rumbling for 537 rushing yards on 6.2 yards per carry while scoring six times-four on the ground and two through the air. Last season's Super Bowl MVP with the Seahawks is earning every penny of his big free-agent contract, and his presence in the backfield is also opening things up for Patrick Mahomes, putting KC in the top five in the NFL in points per game at 29.5 and second in yards per game at 412.0, behind only the Rams. Walker should be able to continue rolling in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Terry McLaurin
roster.outlook: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels returned from injury and appeared to show no ill effects regarding his previously dislocated elbow. Daniels rushed for over 100 yards and two touchdowns, while also passing for 199 yards against the Giants. Unfortunately, poor game management at the end of overtime cost the Commanders the win, and overshadows what was otherwise a solid return to the lineup for Daniels. Unfortunately, a tall task lurks in Week 6 on the road versus the 49ers. San Francisco is undefeated and allowing just 297.2 scrimmage yards per tilt, which is sixth in the league.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will look to continue his dominance as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Watson recorded a stellar performance in Week 5 against the Bears, bringing in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout has cemented himself as Jordan Love's top option in the passing game, with a 26-474-6 receiving line through five games. Watson will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy and the 49ers will look to remain perfect with a Week 6 win over Washington. Purdy was sacked for the first time this season and threw his first pickoff since Week 1 this past Sunday against Seattle, but he also threw two touchdowns to help guide San Francisco to victory. He was especially synched up with veteran wideout Mike Evans, with whom he connected seven times for 113 yards and a score. Purdy could feast on a Commanders defense that has given up 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most in the NFL) and 27.9 fantasy points per game (second-most in the league) to quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.outlook: Dallas Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions last game. Returning from a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert responded with six catches on nine targets. Unfortunately, Goedert gained just 38 yards, and the Eagles lost by a score of 19-17. If both DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley continue to be sidelined due to their respective hamstring injuries, though, Goedert should see plenty of looks, including in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: George Holani
roster.outlook: George Holani will likely need to better protect the ball in Week 6 against the Broncos if he wants to continue getting opportunities in Seattle's ground game. Holani fumbled twice this past Sunday against the 49ers, and the fumble that was recovered by San Francisco was a game-changer, as it resulted in a touchdown just before halftime. With that said, Seattle is depleted at running back with Zach Charbonnet (knee - ACL) out at least another week and Jadrian Price (chest) on IR until at least early November, so Holani should get an opportunity to redeem himself against Denver. The Broncos are giving up 21.1 fantasy points per game to RBs, eighth-most in the league.

roster.name: AJ Barner
roster.outlook: AJ Barner will look to get more involved as a pass catcher for Seattle in Week 6 against the Broncos. Barner caught three of five targets for 20 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, with each of the catch, target and yardage totals representing his second-highest mark this season. Barner logged six receiving touchdowns across 17 regular-season games last year, but his only score this season has been on his lone rush attempt. Denver has struggled a bit against tight ends this season, giving up 9.9 fantasy points per game, ninth-most in the league.

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.outlook: Spencer Shrader has emerged as an elite fantasy kicker through five weeks, converting all 12 of his field-goal attempts over the Colts' last three games. He's 16-for-16 overall this season, including a perfect 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards. Indianapolis' offense generated plenty of field-goal opportunities in the first half of last season before falling off a cliff in the second half, so the risk of regression is substantial. However, Shrader has an excellent opportunity to keep rolling in Week 6 against the winless Titans, who have allowed 13 field goals through five games, tied with Pittsburgh for the most in the NFL. Keep starting Shrader if you have him.

roster.name: Tyler Allgeier
roster.outlook: Tyler Allgeier's role in Arizona's backfield seems to be fading ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Allgeier logged just three carries for seven yards this past Sunday against Detroit while adding nine yards on two catches. The veteran running back has logged three or fewer totes two of the past three weeks and seems to be far behind rookie Jeremiyah Love, who got 12 carries versus the Lions, in the pecking order. With that said, he could get some opportunities as a pass catcher against the Rams, who have given up the fourth-most receiving yards per game (42.6) to running backs through five weeks.

roster.name: Keaton Mitchell
roster.outlook: Keaton Mitchell is coming off a disappointing Week 5 performance against the Broncos, as he turned nine touches into a modest 29 scrimmage yards. He was outgained by both Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal as the Chargers' backfield devolves into a full committee, but none of the three have made a strong case to seize the clear No. 1 role. Mitchell flashed big-play potential during his time with the Ravens, but working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line won't generate many holes. He'll try to produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty continues to keep his production afloat via his skills as a pass-catcher. The second-year running back is averaging just 3.3 yards per carry after another poor showing on the ground in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, but he's supplied a 22-215-2 line on 30 targets through five games. The 30 targets are third in the league among RBs, behind the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs and the Rams' Kyren Williams, while Jeanty's receiving yards are third behind Gibbs and the Steelers' Jaylen Warren. Jeanty will try to deliver a more well-rounded line in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and 31st in receiving TDs allowed to the position.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens travel to take on the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He hauled in eight of nine targets for 53 yards during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Flowers paced the team in receptions and targets and was second in yardage, showing a strong rapport with Tyler Huntley, who started in place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle). No matter who's under center, Flowers remains the top receiving threat against Cleveland's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (36.4) to WRs.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain for Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets due to an ankle injury. When healthy, he hasn't logged more than a 37% snap share in any of the last three games and has only two catches on the season. The Jets have not faced a prolific rushing offense through five games but have allowed two opposing backs to gain at least 99 yards. If active, a split role with Rhamondre Stevenson caps Henderson's appeal against a defense allowing a stingy 4.3 yards per carry.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson is set to lead Arizona's wideout corps versus the Rams in Week 6. After Marvin Harrison was made inactive this past Sunday due to a pending trade, Wilson functioned as the no-doubt No. 1 WR for the Cardinals but managed just four catches for 30 yards against Detroit. He was outproduced by fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne, who posted a 5-70-0 line, but Wilson should have plenty of chances to thrive with Harrison officially off to Houston. The Rams have given up the fewest receiving yards per game to wideouts this season, but they've also surrendered seven receiving TDs to the position, tied for third-most in the league.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.outlook: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.

roster.name: Jerry Jeudy
roster.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Ravens for a divisional clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 19 yards during Cleveland's Week 5 defeat. Jeudy became more involved after KC Concepcion (concussion) exited in the first quarter, and there's a chance the rookie will be unable to clear the NFL's five-step protocol before their matchup with Baltimore. If that is indeed the case, Jeudy will slide into the No. 2 receiver role behind Denzel Boston against a Ravens defense allowing 36.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 23rd.

roster.name: Kayshon Boutte
roster.outlook: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 31 receiving yards per game and has yet to score as a member of the Texans. Houston doesn't seem happy with the August trade acquisition from New England, considering the Texans dipped back into the trade market at wide receiver after their Week 5 win over the Titans and acquired Marvin Harrison from Arizona. Even if Harrison isn't ready to assume a prominent role in Week 6, Boutte hasn't shown enough to warrant fantasy consideration outside the deepest of formats, even in a favorable matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing the most yards per game to wide receivers.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud could have a key new target for Houston's pivotal Week 6 clash with the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London. The Texans are just 1-4 and have already fallen three games behind Jacksonville in the standings, but Stroud is quietly averaging a career-high 280 passing yards per game to go with a 6:0 TD:INT. Jacksonville gives up the fewest rushing yards and second-most passing yards per game, so Stroud will likely be asked to carry Houston's offense again in Week 6, making him a viable starting QB in fantasy. The Texans notched their first win of the season in Week 5 over the Titans and promptly traded for disgruntled Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison, who hasn't lived up to the hype as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft but excelled at Ohio State while catching passes from Stroud in 2022. Harrison likely won't be fully up to speed, but he could still provide an upgrade over Houston's current wideouts behind Nico Collins.

roster.name: Darius Cooper
roster.outlook: Darius Cooper continues to flash his big-play ability for the Eagles. Cooper snagged his fourth touchdown of the season last game versus the Jaguars en route to leading the Eagles in receiving yards. Four of Cooper's seven receptions have gone for touchdowns in 2026. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has also likely boosted the opportunities for Cooper, who has 10 targets in his last two contests alone. This trend could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Chris Boswell
roster.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to battle the Buccaneers in Week 6. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Over his last three outings, Boswell is 6-for-7 on field goals while making all eight of his PATs. He's on the fantasy radar with the recent strong performances by the Steelers offense, as they've averaged 29.3 points during this three-game stretch. Boswell will try to make an impact against a Tampa Bay defense allowing 22.4 points per game in 2026, but just 15.0 PPG over their previous two.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice picked up a minor hamstring strain and was limited to just six snaps in Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Raiders, but coming out of a Week 5 bye, the issue may not cost him any further time. In his first three games of the season, Rice produced a 13-190-1 line on 15 targets, and his volume could increase with speedster Tyquan Thornton out due to an ankle injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the year. Rice could pop for big numbers in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey continues to deal with injuries, sitting out the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a foot issue after dealing with a rib injury earlier in the season. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 3, but in those first three games, McConkey managed a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets as Justin Herbert's clear No. 1 option. The rest of the team's wide receiver room is also banged up, which could give the team extra incentive to get McConkey back in the lineup as quickly as possible. Even if he suits up in Week 6, he'll struggle to contribute against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery is considered week-to-week after departing Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. He's likely to sit out in Week 6 against the Jaguars, leaving Woody Marks to lead Houston's backfield against Jacksonville's league-best run defense in London. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.

roster.name: Zach Charbonnet
roster.outlook: Zach Charbonnet continues to rehab from a torn ACL and isn't expected to play in Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver. Charbonnet did have his 21-day practice window opened last week, and he got in a couple limited practice sessions, but the fact that the Seahawks are playing on Thursday night this week complicates his outlook for a return to action. As such, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani are slated to lead Seattle's RB corps again. Charbonnet does have a chance to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against Kansas City.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks is set to lead Houston's backfield in Week 6 against the Jaguars, as fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) is considered week-to-week. Marks racked up 85 scrimmage yards on 19 touches in the Week 5 win over Tennessee, a game Montgomery exited in the first half. Jacksonville is allowing a league-low 63.8 rushing yards per game, but RBs are averaging 40 receiving yards per game against the Jaguars. Expectations should be tempered due to the difficult matchup, but Marks is projected to get plenty of touches, making him a high-end Week 6 flex option.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara is expected to remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite operating as New Orleans' No. 1 RB over the last two weeks, Kamara logged fewer snaps (12) and carries (three) than Kendre Miller (six carries on 13 snaps) in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings. Additionally, he got fewer targets than Miller (two to three), which is a very negative sign for his outlook going forward. Even so, Kamara could be productive against a Giants defense that's given up just 94 receiving yards but two receiving touchdowns to RBs this season.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.

roster.name: Hunter Henry
roster.outlook: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.

roster.name: Bo Nix
roster.outlook: Bo Nix didn't show any improvement in Week 5 as the Broncos switched back to Sean Payton as their play-caller, throwing for a season-low 123 yards and producing just one touchdown in a win over the Chargers. The third-year QB has a meager 6:3 TD:INT through five games and is completing fewer than 60.0% of his passes, averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. There's still reason to believe Nix's numbers will improve once Payton gets back in a rhythm, but the Denver offense's ceiling seems limited even if it's operating at peak efficiency. Nix isn't likely to break out in Week 6 against a Seahawks defense that ranks sixth this season in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the division rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He tallied 14 carries for 44 yards and caught three of four targets for six yards during Cleveland's Week 5 loss. Judkins played just 52.9% of snaps, likely due to a right ankle injury suffered in-game, and he was reportedly spotted wearing a walking boot afterward. Head coach Todd Monken called it a "tweak" on Monday and considers his starting running back day-to-day. Judkins' practice participation this week will be worth monitoring, as he'll be facing a Baltimore defense that allows 18.8 fantasy points per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Pitts had his best game of the 2026 season during the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, catching five of six targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. Since the return of quarterback Michael Penix (ribs) in Week 3, Pitts has caught nine of 11 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown. Pitts could struggle in Week 6, however, as he's set to face a Chicago defense that's allowed just 7.7 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson could garner workhorse carries in the Patriots' Week 6 match against the Jets with TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an ankle issue. Stevenson had 13 carries in Week 5 for the second straight week and now has double-digit carries in three of five games while adding at least three catches four times. With double-digit touches seemingly certain, Stevenson can exploit a defense that's allowing 4.3 yards per carry and one where he posted 102 yards and two touchdowns on only 13 touches last season.

roster.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
roster.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

roster.name: Matt Gay
roster.outlook: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.

roster.name: Tyler Higbee
roster.outlook: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.

roster.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Jaleel McLaughlin and the Browns return home to host the Ravens in Week 6. He did not record a carry and failed to bring in his lone target during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. McLaughlin has rushed twice for 31 yards and one touchdown across four outings so far in 2026. However, he could see an increase in playing time as the only healthy Cleveland running back against Baltimore's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.8). Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) are both dealing with injuries, and Dylan Sampson (knee) remains on injured reserve. It's probably best to avoid everyone outside of Judkins in fantasy, assuming he's active, in what could be a murky backfield rotation.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook will seek the end zone for the fifth straight week when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. While Cook hasn't been heavily targeted in the passing game, he's posted 100-plus yard rushing efforts in three of his last four outings, garnering at least 21 carries at the same rate. Buffalo is a run-first offense, and the Week 6 matchup is very appealing; Las Vegas allows 5.2 yards per carry, again setting up Cook to be a top-tier option.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.outlook: Jeremiyah Love will look to rebound in Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams. Love managed just 22 yards on 12 carries against Detroit this past Sunday, and he finished without a catch for the first time as a pro. The rookie continues to lead the Cardinals' ground attack but has managed a meager 3.7 yards per carry through five weeks. The Rams rank 12th in the NFL by giving up 15.5 fantasy points per game to running backs.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets.
