After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle should be past an illness by the time the 49ers face Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 6. Kittle suited up this past Sunday against Seattle despite falling under the weather near game day. He ended up with a modest five catches on six targets for 24 yards but logged his usual big workload with a season-high 93 percent offensive snap share. Kittle could be primed for a big game against the Commanders, who have surrendered 15.8 fantasy points per game -- second-most in the league -- to tight ends.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum's role as a ball carrier seems to fading ahead of the Rams' Week 6 game versus Arizona. Corum rushed just five times for 19 yards Monday against Buffalo, marking his third straight contest with six or fewer carries after averaging 11 totes across the first two weeks. However, Corum did score his first TD of 2026 and had easily his best game this season as a receiver against the Bills, catching three passes for 53 yards. Given his recent downturn in carries, Corum may need to get into the end zone to come away with serviceable fantasy production, but the Cardinals have given up only four total TDs to running backs through five weeks this season.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker's opportunities continue to be inconsistent due to the struggles of the Chargers' offense. The kicker hasn't attempted more than two PATs in any of the team's first five games, going a perfect 9-for-9, and he's seen one or fewer field goal attempts in three of those five contests. With the offensive line in shambles and Justin Herbert running out of healthy targets, Dicker's volume doesn't seem likely to pick up anytime soon. He'll face a Kansas City squad in Week 6 that's allowing 19.3 points per game, seventh in the league.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange became the latest TE to take advantage of a Bengals defense that has allowed the most yards in the league to the position. He compiled 95 receiving yards in Week 4 against Cincinnati to lead the Jaguars. Strange had recorded just 72 yards over the preceding three games combined, and he's likely to return to a reduced role in Week 5 against an Eagles defense that's holding TEs to 39 yards per game and has yet to allow a TD to the position. While Strange can be worth streaming in the right matchups, Week 5 isn't one of them.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.

roster.name: Jalen Hurts
roster.outlook: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are on the road to take on the Buccaneers in Week 6. He caught three of four targets for 12 yards and rushed once for 11 yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Metcalf and Darnell Washington tied for the fewest receiving yards on the team, while the veteran wideout finished fourth in targets. He'll try to rebound against a Tampa Bay defense that allows 29.5 fantasy points per game (12th) to WRs and just gave up nine receptions for 130 yards and a TD to George Pickens.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid's role in the Bills' passing game is shrinking ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. After snagging 12 of 14 targets in his first two games, Kincaid has been limited to four catches on seven targets over the last three weeks, amassing just 52 yards. His snap share remains strong and elevated from 2025; Buffalo just seems more inclined to be a run-first offense. Las Vegas has allowed six touchdowns to opposing tight ends, resulting in the fifth-most fantasy points allowed to the position. Kincaid can be a viable starting option in a favorable bounce-back matchup.

roster.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson was ineffective in the Week 5 overtime loss, accumulating just 16 yards on seven carries (2.3 yards per carry). Through five contests this season, Robinson has averaged 42 rushing yards per game, with most of his value coming from touchdowns (four on the season). He could struggle in Week 6 against a Bears defense that's given up just 409 rushing yards to RBs this season.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers is coming off a huge fantasy performance with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in the Denver altitude on tap. Myers made all five of his field-goal tries and both of his extra-point attempts in a loss to San Francisco this past Sunday, with all five of his FGs coming from 40-plus yards. Fantasy managers who roster Myers were likely waiting for this type of performance, as the veteran kicker had attempted (and made) only five field goals combined over the first four weeks of the campaign. Opponents are 9-for-11 in FG attempts against the Broncos this season.

roster.name: Keon Coleman
roster.outlook: Keon Coleman brings inconsistent volume in the Bills' passing game into a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Coleman saw just two targets in Week 5 despite the absence of DJ Moore, marking the third time in five outings he's drawn that limited amount of volume. Buffalo remains a run-first offense and while Coleman has shown red zone and downfield ability, the lack of consistent volume leads to volatility against a Las Vegas secondary that's allowing the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts, though has been more vulnerable over the middle of late than to boundary receivers.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.outlook: Jordan Love will look to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Love was on fire in a blowout win over the Bears in Week 5, completing 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. After a shaky but still touchdown-heavy start to the season, he's now completed 73 percent or more of his passes in back-to-back weeks and totaled 564 passing yards with a 4:1 TD:INT ratio in that stretch. Love will have the perfect opportunity to replicate his greatness again, as Dallas has ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks (23.8) so far this season.

free_agents.name: Jakobi Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.

free_agents.name: Harrison Butker
free_agents.outlook: Harrison Butker has been more floor than ceiling to begin the season. The Kansas City kicker has kicked at least three extra points in all four games, but he's logged more than one field goal only once, going 7-for-9 over that span with both his misses coming from 50-plus yards. With Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker having the offense operating at a very high level, Butker's mix of opportunities isn't likely to change much. He could be busy in Week 6 against a Chargers team allowing 25.8 points per game, tied for 22nd in the league.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins' production is declining, potentially reducing his time as the Raiders' starting quarterback. After throwing for nine touchdowns during the team's 3-0 start to the season, the veteran has a 3:1 TD:INT over the last two contests, both losses. During a lopsided Week 5 loss to the Patriots, Cousins ceded the final drive to prized rookie Fernando Mendoza, which could be the first step toward Mendoza taking the reins. Cousins' job doesn't seem to be in immediate peril, and he could bounce back in a big way in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Justin Herbert
free_agents.outlook: Justin Herbert and the Chargers remain winless after a Week 5 loss to the Broncos, as their season spirals down the drain. Injuries have once again gutted the offensive line, with left tackle Rashawn Slater joining center Tyler Biadasz on IR, but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel also doesn't seem to have any answers. Herbert has posted a career-low 59.4% completion rate and 6.6 yards per attempt through five games with a woeful 5:7 TD:INT, and now his top four wide receivers, along with tight end David Njoku, are all injured. Herbert doesn't seem likely to turn things around in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top safety blanket in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Godwin has caught 19 of 22 targets this season, totaling 179 yards. Despite ranking second on the Buccaneers in receptions and third in targets, he's gotten just one red-zone target all season and could struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. Regardless, Godwin is in for a tough Week 6 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up 220.8 passing yards per game this year.

free_agents.name: Jameis Winston
free_agents.outlook: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns for the second-consecutive week for the Giants. He also threw for over 300 yards for the first time this season in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders.  Winston did not throw a pick, though he did lose a fumble. While JJ McCarthy took a few snaps, the starting job will remain Winston's heading into a Week 6 clash with the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston was unable to play through a chest injury in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, missing his first game of the season. The fourth-year wideout has just a 7-108-0 line on 19 targets in four contests, and the team's offensive struggles under coordinator Mike McDaniel have dragged down essentially every skill player on the roster. If Johnston returns in Week 6, it will be for a brutal matchup against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Kendre Miller
free_agents.outlook: Kendre Miller is expected to remain a large part of the Saints' rushing attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Miller operated as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, receiving more carries (six) and targets (three) while playing more snaps (13) than Alvin Kamara (three carries and two targets on 12 snaps). While Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains sidelined, Miller appears to have assumed the role as the Saints' top rusher. He could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's given up 21.3 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears had a season-high 11 touches, including nine catches, in Tennessee's Week 5 loss to the Texans. His contributions as a receiver give Spears some deep-league flex appeal for Week 6 against a Colts defense that's allowing a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to running backs. Tony Pollard remains the top backfield option in a low-octane Titans offense that's scoring a league-low 11.6 points per game, while Spears has only one game with more than 28 scrimmage yards this season.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz leads the Texans with 24 catches heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Jaguars in London, though half of those receptions came in Week 2 against the Bengals. Jacksonville has been among the five stingiest defenses against TEs, limiting the position to 3.6 catches for 34 yards per game. The Jaguars have allowed two TDs to the position, but Schultz has scored only five times in 39 regular-season games since the start of the 2024 season and is still searching for his first TD of the season. Despite Schultz's respectable target volume, he's best left on the bench in single-TE formats in Week 6.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed has been a relatively quiet contributor to Seattle's passing game heading into a Week 6 tilt in Denver. Shaheed has caught three or fewer passes in all of the Seahawks' games so far this season and has yet to record a receiving touchdown, though he does have rushing score on his ledger. The speedy wideout has a big role as an electric kick returner, but Shaheed may struggle to produce as a pass catcher as long as Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to eat up targets. The Broncos are giving up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (16.3) to wideouts this season, but they could be without both starting cornerbacks -- Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) -- in Week 6.

free_agents.name: Harrison Mevis
free_agents.outlook: Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his first three-TD performance of the campaign heading into Arizona's Week 6 clash against the Rams. Two of Brissett's scores in this past Sunday's blowout loss to Detroit came after the outcome was already decided, but they count the same in the world of fantasy football. The veteran quarterbacks also threw for a season-high 292 yards and rushed for a season-best 19 yards, though he did throw his fifth interception of the campaign. Brissett could find the sledding tougher against the Rams, who have given up just 5.65 yards per attempt this season, second-best in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Travis Hunter
free_agents.outlook: Travis Hunter got his first offensive touch since Week 1 during the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Eagles, but he's being used as a full-time defensive player while barely seeing the field on offense. Barring a rash of injuries at wide receiver, the Jaguars will likely remain content using Hunter primarily at cornerback. He has enough talent to warrant a bench stash if you have space on the roster, but he isn't an appealing fantasy option in Week 6 against the Texans unless your league counts defensive contributions.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day return window opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans and has rejoined his teammates at practice but remains on injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to London to face the Jaguars. Considering the Texans just traded for WR Marvin Harrison, Dell seems unlikely to be a major contributor in Week 6, even if he is activated from IR. Dell isn't viable in Week 6 but could be worth stashing if you have an open bench or IR slot, as Houston's 2023 third-round pick averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to sustaining a major knee injury late in the 2024 season.

free_agents.name: Aaron Rodgers
free_agents.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He threw for 235 yards (22-for-31) with three TDs and no INTs while rushing once for six yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. That's three straight weeks that the 42-year-old has tossed three scores, and he now has a 10:4 TD:INT through five games this season. Rodgers looks to stay hot versus a stingy Buccaneers defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points allowed to QBs (18.4 per game).

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Chase McLaughlin
free_agents.outlook: Chase McLaughlin will look to stay hot in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. McLaughlin impressed during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, converting on his lone field-goal try and all three point-after attempts. He remains perfect on the season, making all 20 of his kicks this season (10 field goals and 10 extra points). He could have plenty of scoring chances against a Steelers defense that's given up 9.8 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tyler Bass
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing six times for 40 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Watson was sacked eight times for 53 yards and fumbled three times, although he recovered two of them. After leading the Browns to a three-game win streak behind strong performances, Watson struggled with pressure and the rainy conditions in the Week 5 defeat. He'll aim to bounce back versus Baltimore's 12th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington logged a season-low two touches in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, turning one carry and one reception into just 10 scrimmage yards. Ashton Jeanty continues to get a bell-cow workload despite his struggles on the ground, and Washington's 5.0 yards per carry on the season might encourage coach Klint Kubiak to give him more work on early downs. The rookie has flashed his big-play potential, but until he gets more consistent volume, his main value will be as injury insurance behind Jeanty. Washington may not need many touches to contribute in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones has just a 3:4 TD:INT and hasn't rushed for more than 10 yards in a game heading into the Colts' Week 6 home game against the Titans. Indianapolis' offense relies primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and that formula is unlikely to change since the Colts will likely have the luxury of playing from ahead in Week 6 against a Titans team that has been outscored 109-58 this season but allowed only five passing TDs. Between Jones' own limitations as a passer and his team's lack of receiving talent, he remains an unappetizing Week 6 fantasy option, even in superflex and multi-QB formats.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving tight end during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite signing with the Panthers in early August, Waller ranks first amongst the team's tight end corps in targets (19), receptions (13), yards (148) and touchdowns (two) through four games. Waller could receive fewer opportunities in Week 6, however, with Jalen Coker (quadriceps) expected to return from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a difficult matchup against an Eagles defense that's allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught five of six targets for 62 yards during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. Bateman led the team in receiving yards and was second in receptions while tying for second in targets. Tyler Huntley, who started for Lamar Jackson (ankle), attempted 32 passes and relied heavily on the wideout, as all five of Bateman's catches resulted in first downs for the Ravens. He'll aim to make a similar difference against a Browns defense allowing 36.4 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 24th.

free_agents.name: Michael Mayer
free_agents.outlook: Michael Mayer's volume took a significant step backward in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After turning 10 targets into an 8-82-0 line in Week 4, Mayer got only one look from Kirk Cousins in New England, turning it into a two-yard gain. Brock Bowers is the unquestioned top option in the team's passing game, but a lack of established wide receivers has created an opening for Mayer to be more than just injury insurance. Through five games, he's delivered a 21-171-1 line on 25 targets, putting him on pace for career-best numbers in 2026. Mayer will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Emmett Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Emmett Johnson has seen little work to begin his career as the No. 2 running back for Kansas City behind bell cow Kenneth Walker. Johnson is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but the fifth-round rookie has teased his big-play potential as a pass catcher, catching all five of his targets for 74 yards. As long as Walker remains healthy, Johnson will remain little more than an upside bench stash. He could get some garbage-time touches in Week 6 against a Chargers defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.

free_agents.name: Roman Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Roman Wilson and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He failed to catch his only target prior to exiting Pittsburgh's 34-22 win in Week 5 with a finger injury. Wilson has already been ruled out for the trip to Tampa Bay, meaning Germie Bernard should see a boost in playing time and opportunities in his absence.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez has exceeded six rushing attempts in only one of five games with the Jaguars and has just one catch all season. With starting RB Bhayshul Tuten healthy heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Texans, Rodriguez doesn't look like a usable fantasy option in most formats against a stout Houston front seven that's limiting RBs to 3.5 yards per carry. Rodriguez remains a viable bench stash for managers hedging against a Tuten injury.

free_agents.name: Trey Smack
free_agents.outlook: Trey Smack will aim to get back on track as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Smack's accuracy was not on point against the Bears in Week 5, as he went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on XPAs. While the rookie kicker's struggles didn't matter in an eventual blowout win, he'll need to get better when high-importance kicks come up more later in the year. Smack will face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack (8.0 points allowed per game) versus fantasy kickers this year.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix (ribs) will lead the Falcons' passing attack if active during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Penix was productive for the third consecutive game before exiting with a rib injury in the overtime loss to the Ravens, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. Through three weeks, Penix is averaging 239.7 passing yards and a touchdown per game. He's in for a favorable matchup if ready for Week 6, as the Bears' defense just allowed Jordan Love to throw for 367 yards and two touchdowns.

free_agents.name: Will Shipley
free_agents.outlook: Will Shipley found the end zone last game for the Eagles but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Pierre Strong could serve as Green Bay's secondary option at running back once again in Week 6 against the Cowboys. With Chris Brooks on IR with an ankle injury, Strong was brought up for Week 5 versus the Bears. The fourth-year ball carrier ended up serving as the Packers' No. 2 option instead of Kaleb Johnson, with MarShawn Lloyd leading the ground attack. Strong recorded five carries for seven yards and three catches for 11 yards off four targets. If the hierarchy stays the same, he could be in for another game of solid usage facing a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal posted a season-high nine touches in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, turning eight carries into 57 yards and his first rushing touchdown of the season while also catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. The third-year back has gotten into the end zone in back-to-back games, but Vidal remains firmly in a committee with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell, and none of the three would seem to have a significant ceiling while working behind a patchwork offensive line. Vidal will try to keep his TD streak going in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver on tap. Kupp has produced a modest 11 catches for 129 yards and a touchdown through five weeks, and he's posted just three catches for 28 yards in his past two games. He's regularly logging a healthy offensive snap share, but there hasn't been much room for any of Seattle's complementary wideouts to shine behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 10.0 targets per game. Kupp may need a big play or two to break out, but the Broncos are yielding just 7.65 yards per WR target, 12th-best in the league.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk will likely continue having scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Folk was perfect in the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, making three field goals and two extra points. On the season, he's converted on nine of 12 field-goal tries but all 12 of his point-after attempts. He could have plenty of scoring chance in Week 6, as Chicago's defense just allowed 31 points while Packers' kicker Trey Smack attempted six kicks (three field goals and three extra points).

free_agents.name: Najee Harris
free_agents.outlook: Najee Harris had five carries for just nine yards last game for the Giants. The running game as a whole was fairly contained, as starter Cam Skattebo rushed for just 58 yards in the 27-27 tie with Washington. Interestingly, Tyrone Tracy also had five touches in this contest, perhaps showing that the backup role remains up for grabs. In Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He rushed four times for 73 yards and caught two of four targets for five yards during Baltimore's Week 5 overtime win. Derrick Henry out-carried him 24-4, although Hill led the way with a game-long 47-yard run. However, as long as Henry is the lead back and the Ravens don't fall into a massive deficit, Hill's involvement in the offense will remain limited.

free_agents.name: Dylan Sampson
free_agents.outlook: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley hasn't exceeded 35 yards in a game this season and has been blanked twice. The 31-year-old wide receiver appears to have lost a step after fracturing his fibula last season and has fallen to No. 4 on Tennessee's wide receiver depth chart behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, and Elic Ayomanor. With QB Cam Ward averaging a meager 179 passing yards per game, Ridley is unlikely to post his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season in Week 6, even against the Colts' subpar secondary.

free_agents.name: Kendrick Bourne
free_agents.outlook: Kendrick Bourne seems set for a major role in Arizona's offense ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. With Marvin Harrison now officially traded to the Texans, Bourne figures to slot in behind Michael Wilson as the Cardinals' No. 2 wideout. That positioning led to a nice game for Bourne this past Sunday against Detroit, as he outproduced Wilson with a 5-70-0 line on eight targets. The Rams could present a challenge, however, as they've yielded the fewest catches per game (8.0) to wideouts through five weeks.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott connected on his lone field goal attempt last game for the Eagles. Elliott made a 48-yarder that initially looked like the game-winner, only for Philadelphia to somehow squander away the victory. Elliott has hit one field goal or fewer in all but one game in 2026, as the Eagles offense has struggled due to injury and inconsistency. However, in Week 6, the Eagles will face a Panthers squad allowing 27.3 points per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith faces an uphill battle for fantasy success when the Jets face the Patriots in Week 6. Smith has been held to 182 yards or fewer in consecutive weeks and has multiple touchdown passes just once through five games. While the Patriots' secondary is banged up, they've still allowed just a 6:3 TD:INT ratio through five games while holding three quarterbacks to no more than 187 yards. The Jets hope to remain run-first, limiting Smith's opportunities.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields saw just two targets last game for the Giants. Meanwhile, star teammate Malik Nabers had a staggering 20 looks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. The production for the rookie Fields has been rather consistent through five contests, as he has two catches in every outing. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Antonio Williams
free_agents.outlook: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tyler Huntley
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens travel to Cleveland for a Week 6 AFC North showdown. In place of the injured Lamar Jackson (ankle) in Week 5, Huntley threw for 201 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 20 yards and another score, helping Baltimore escape with a 30-23 overtime victory. Jackson's availability against the Browns' 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to QBs is still in question, so keep an eye on his practice participation leading up to Week 6. If the Ravens opt to play it safe with their superstar quarterback, Huntley could again be tasked with leading the offense as they look to improve to 5-1 on the season.

free_agents.name: Cam Ward
free_agents.outlook: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel continues to make the most of his opportunities for the Texans. The 2025 third-round pick has caught every pass thrown his way in four of five games this season, leads the team with 17.5 yards per catch and just scored his first TD of the campaign while tying his season high with five targets in the Week 5 win over Tennessee. Noel's arrow is pointing up ahead of a Week 6 matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing a league-high 204 receiving yards per game to WRs, though his floor remains low due to modest volume, as he has earned just 17 targets through five games. He's a boom-or-bust Week 6 flex option for managers in deeper leagues or in search of a bye-week plug-in.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz has missed field goal attempts in the Broncos' last two games, but he's also benefited from increased volume, going 5-for-7 on FGs and 2-for-2 on PATs. The veteran kicker has had his production dragged down by the struggles of the offense, but with Sean Payton calling plays again, Lutz's outlook has brightened a little. He'll face a Seahawks team in Week 6 that's allowed 21.0 points per game this season, eighth in the league.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor sat out the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots with a concussion, but his absence may not last much longer. Whether he finds a bigger role in the game plan is another question. The former Viking has caught just five of 11 targets for 52 yards through four games, and his primary value in Klint Kubiak's offensive scheme seems to be as a blocker. Las Vegas doesn't have a true No. 1 wide receiver, with tight end Brock Bowers serving as Kirk Cousins' top option, so the door is still open for Nailor to work his way up in the pecking order. Assuming he's cleared to return, he'll get a great opportunity in Week 6 against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris wasn't able to take advantage of the absences of Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He played 30 snaps, catching two of four targets for 16 yards before also getting hurt. Harris is viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but he was already struggling to make an impression in a Mike McDaniel scheme that is performing well below expectations in all areas. If Harris does get cleared to play in Week 6, he'll be facing a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Otton had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching three of four targets for 25 yards. However, he ranks second on the Buccaneers in targets (27) and receiving yards (182) through five games, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Pittsburgh defense that's given up 13.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday in Week 6 as the Bears play the Falcons. Johnson got solid opportunities in Chicago's Week 5 blowout loss to Green Bay, with Kyle Monangai out with a toe injury, rushing the ball five times for six yards and reeling in five of seven targets for 34 yards. Johnson's receiving upside could keep him relevant again if Monangai remains sidelined. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 21st in receiving yards allowed to RBs this season.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland is coming off back-to-back quiet weeks with Arizona's Week 6 matchup against the Rams on tap. Ryland has gone just 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts over his past two games, though he's made all six of his extra-point tries during that span. The veteran kicker does have two games with at least three FG makes on the campaign, so it's been pretty feast or famine in terms of his opportunities so far. Opponents are 9-for-11 on field-goal tries against the Rams so far this season.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Mason will remain sidelined for Week 6 as the Packers take on the Cowboys. Brooks is currently on IR due to an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next three weeks. His absence from the field sets up MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong as Green Bay's running back options in the near future.

free_agents.name: Fernando Mendoza
free_agents.outlook: Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action late in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards. His lone drive stalled in the red zone after he came up just short on a fourth-and-4 scramble. Kirk Cousins has led the team to a 3-2 record and remains the starter, but after Las Vegas used the first overall pick in the 2026 draft on Mendoza, it's only a matter of time before he gets a proper look under center. Another loss or two, something that seems very possible given the Raiders' upcoming schedule, could prompt coach Klint Kubiak to make the switch. If Mendoza does see action again in Week 6, he could pop for some intriguing numbers against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to bounce back from a poor performance in Carolina's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite an upset win over the Lions in Week 4, Fitzgerald made just two of four point-after attempts. On the season, the second-year pro has made all nine field goals but has struggled on extra points, converting on just 10 of 13 tries. He's in for a tougher Week 6 matchup as well, with Philadelphia's defense allowing just 6.8 kicking pints per game this year.

free_agents.name: Chig Okonkwo
free_agents.outlook: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ty Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Ty Johnson will look to again create chunk plays in the passing game when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Johnson has only one carry in three games, but for the second time this season, he snagged four passes, finishing with 72 yards in Week 5. Johnson's role appears clear, and he's unlikely to have the chance to exploit a Las Vegas defense that's allowing 5.2 yards per carry but has been stingy to running backs in the passing game, surrendering just 29 receiving yards per game.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.

free_agents.name: Oronde Gadsden
free_agents.outlook: Oronde Gadsden may need a trade to reclaim the fantasy value he displayed as a rookie in 2025. Even with the Chargers' wide receiver room depleted by injuries in Week 5, the second-year tight end notched just one target in a loss to the Broncos, while veteran Charlie Kolar turned four looks from Justin Herbert into three catches for a team-high 37 yards. Gadsden is the more dangerous pass catcher, but coordinator Mike McDaniel doesn't trust him with blocking assignments and apparently doesn't see much in him as a downfield option either. If Gadsden can work his way into a larger role, he could produce in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Efton Chism III
free_agents.outlook: Efton Chism aims to continue ascending the Patriots receiver depth chart Week 6 against the Jets. Chism has 10 targets over the last two weeks with both Mack Hollins and A.J. Brown sidelined, compiling 97 yards and a touchdown. Drake Maye is spreading targets, making Chism a touch volatile, but facing a Jets defense that's allowed four opposing receivers to go for 63 yards or more in two weeks offers Chism the potential to keep it going.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram is coming off his most productive game of the season in terms of receiving yards in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers. With Sean Payton calling plays again, the veteran tight end caught all four of his targets for 55 yards. Engram remains a secondary option in the passing game behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton, but he could get more consistent volume with Payton at the helm. Engram will face a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Isaiah Davis
free_agents.outlook: Isaiah Davis hasn't factored into the Jets' running plans despite Breece Hall's absence entering a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Davis has played a mere 11 offensive snaps in two games, rushing for eight yards on two carries while adding a nine-yard catch. Even if Hall doesn't return in Week 6, Davis would need further injury to Braelon Allen to collect enough touches to succeed against a run defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry.

free_agents.name: Kaleb Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Kaleb Johnson is likely to be a depth option once again as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. After committing a costly goal-line fumble against the Buccaneers in Week 4, Johnson operated as the No. 3 running back for Green Bay in Week 5. The second-year ball carrier was on the field for just nine offensive snaps, and his seven carries for 26 yards came in garbage time. He'll look to make the most of what could be limited opportunities versus a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm remains a fantasy non-factor heading into Week 6 against the Colts, as Tennessee's starting TE is averaging just 12 receiving yards per game. Helm has played over 70% of offensive snaps in every game this season, but he's used primarily as a blocker. The Colts are tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to TEs with four, but Helm has scored only twice through 21 career NFL appearances.

free_agents.name: Brandin Cooks
free_agents.outlook: Brandin Cooks could have an elevated role for San Francisco in Week 6 against the Commanders. Cooks made his first catch for the 49ers this past Sunday against Seattle, hauling in a seven-yard touchdown from QB Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout ended up logging a 38 percent offensive snap share, largely as a result of Deebo Samuel exiting with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. Should Samuel be sidelined in Week 6, Cooks could start at WR alongside Mike Evans. The 49ers' wideout corps could thrive against a Washington defense that has given up seven receiving TDs to the position -- tied for third-most in the NFL -- through six weeks.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to square off against the 1-4 Buccaneers in Week 6. He played 34 snaps on offense (63%) en route to catching two of three targets for 12 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Fellow starting tight end Pat Freiermuth was on the field for 38 offensive snaps (70%) and was the more productive of the two, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two TDs. The playing time will continue to be relatively similar, making Washington a boom-or-bust fantasy option against Tampa Bay's 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.7) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Jalon Daniels
free_agents.outlook: Jalon Daniels is expected to start at quarterback as the Buccaneers' take on the Steelers in Week 6. Daniels has impressed while filling in for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) over the last two weeks, totaling 424 yards and two touchdowns. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Friday that he plans to start Daniels in Week 6, as Tampa Bay continues to be cautious with Mayfield's injury. If Daniels starts as expected, he could struggle against a good Steelers defense that's given up just 16.8 points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Daniel Carlson
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Carlson could see few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Carlson struggled in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, converting on just one of two point-after attempts. On the season, Carlson had made five of seven field-goal tries and 11 of 13 extra-point attempts. He could continue to struggle in Week 6 against a Giants team that's allowed just 4.0 kicking points per game this season, the fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jalen Royals
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Royals could be headed for a big opportunity coming out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye. With Tyquan Thornton likely out for the season due to an ankle injury in a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Royals could emerge as Patrick Mahomes' preferred deep option while Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Travis Kelce handle underneath routes. That role allowed Thornton to erupt for a 5-111-2 line prior to getting hurt against Las Vegas, and Royals showed similar big-play ability in college. The 2025 fourth-round pick will be a very intriguing dart throw in Week 6 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Zachariah Branch
free_agents.outlook: Zachariah Branch will likely play a complimentary role in Atlanta's receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Branch has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching all four of his targets for 25 yards. He appears to have overtaken Olamide Zaccheaus in the wide-receiver room but likely won't have much fantasy value without scoring a touchdown. That being said, Branch could succeed against a Bears defense that's giving up 10.4 yards per target to opposing WRs this season, the most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin saw a season-high four targets last game for the Cowboys.  CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to the additional looks for Turpin. However, Turpin managed just two catches for 22 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Turpin back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson will likely play a depth role on Atlanta's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Dotson has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching four of seven targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. However, he remains firmly behind Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson as pass catchers, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Even so, Dotson could have plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 6, as Chicago's defense has already allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.

free_agents.name: Isaiah Williams
free_agents.outlook: Isaiah Williams' role in the Jets offense may be declining ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Despite Adonai Mitchell's three-week absence, Williams has not logged more than three targets, and his snap share fell to a season-low 59% in Week 5 with the return of Tim Patrick. The Jets aren't throwing the ball enough to sustain secondary pass-catching options, and New England is allowing just 7.5 yards per target, the ninth-lowest in the league, leaving Williams with minimal appeal.

free_agents.name: Darnell Mooney
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Mooney saw seven targets for the Giants last game. Unfortunately, Mooney dropped a couple of passes and failed to connect with quarterback Jameis Winston on some others.  Mooney finished with two catches for just 14 yards, and has just eight receptions on the season. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Kyle Williams
free_agents.outlook: Kyle Williams hopes to maintain his big-play ability in Week 6 when the Patriots host the Jets. Williams hauled in three passes for 91 yards in Week 5, despite a 32% snap share even with Mack Hollins's absence, making Williams reliant on chunk plays for fantasy production. The Jets have allowed just 644 yards to opposing wideouts over five games (128.8 per game), and with New England spreading targets, Williams won't have volume on his side in Week 6.

free_agents.name: Andre Szmyt
free_agents.outlook: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host Baltimore for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He went 2-for-2 on field goals but missed his only extra-point try in Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. The PAT miss was Szmyt's first of the season, and he's now a perfect 10-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-8 on extra points. The Browns' offense took a step back after a three-game winning streak, but some of that can be attributed to the rainy conditions all afternoon. Either way, Szmyt will aim to contribute at home against a Ravens defense allowing 23.8 points per game.

free_agents.name: Tyson Bagent
free_agents.outlook: Tyson Bagent's role is up in the air for Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Bagent got the start in Week 5 against the Packers, but a 57 percent completion rate for 87 yards and a 0:2 TD:INT eventually got him benched for veteran Case Keenum, who didn't fare much better. If Caleb Williams sits out another game with his hamstring injury, it's unknown if the Bears will roll with Bagent or Keenum. If Bagent does see the field, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson may have officially fallen behind Tyler Higbee in Los Angeles' tight-end pecking order heading into a matchup versus the Cardinals in Week 6. Parkinson logged just one catch on two targets for three yards Monday against Buffalo while Higbee went off again with a 5-83-0 receiving line on six targets. The good news for Parkinson is that he was able to suit up following a one-week absence, but he's yet to register more than two catches in a game so far this season. With that in mind, he could struggle to produce in Week 6 despite facing an Arizona defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points per game (13.3) to tight ends through five weeks.

free_agents.name: Jacob Cowing
free_agents.outlook: Jacob Cowing may be in for a bigger role on offense for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Deebo Samuel suffered an injured hamstring versus Seattle this past Sunday, and if he's out versus the Commanders, Cowing should be slated for a key role in the team's passing game. He's yet to make much of an impact so far with just one catch on five targets for nine yards, but there could be room for him to succeed against Washington. The Commanders are surrendering 14.6 receptions per game to wideouts, tied for second-most in the league.

free_agents.name: Cole Kmet
free_agents.outlook: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option in Chicago's passing game during Week 6 at Atlanta. Kmet recorded another catch in Week 5 against the Packers, bringing in one of two targets for eight yards. The veteran tight end has now logged five catches for 56 yards and a touchdown across five games this season. He'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy TEs this year.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens missed an extra point last game for Washington. With the contest resulting in a 27-27 tie, Stevens could have been viewed as the goat. However, late-game clock mismanagement by the offense failed to allow Stevens a chance at redemption, as the Commanders could not get off a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired in overtime. Stevens did hit two other field goals as well as another extra point in the contest. His job should still be safe heading into Week 6 versus the 49ers. However, his opportunities could be limited, as San Fran is yielding just 18.6 points per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurts will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Hurst went without a target for the first time in his NFL career during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys. On the season, the rookie wideout has caught eight of 16 targets for 128 yards and a touchdown, averaging 16.0 yards per reception. He could find success against a solid Steelers secondary in Week 6 that's allowed 10.8 yards per completion this season.

free_agents.name: Case Keenum
free_agents.outlook: Case Keenum usage is up in the air for Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Keenum entered Week 5 versus the Packers as the backup quarterback, but he ended up coming in and completing 11 of 19 passes for 108 yards and one interception after Tyson Bagent's struggles. While Keenum didn't fair that much better than Bagent, the Bears might want to rely on a veteran play caller if Caleb Williams misses another week with a hamstring injury. If Keenum does draw the start, he'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Laquon Treadwell
free_agents.outlook: Laquon Treadwell has been targeted 14 times in the last two games and remains the Colts' No. 3 healthy WR heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans, who rank among the 10 weakest units at preventing catches and yards for wideouts. Treadwell's recent usage and the favorable matchup make him a viable deep-league dart throw, but expectations should be tempered considering the 31-year-old veteran hasn't scored a TD since 2021 and has just five touchdowns in 98 career regular-season appearances. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are likely to continue outperforming Treadwell while the Colts remain without their leading 2025 receiver Alec Pierce (heel).

free_agents.name: Joshua Palmer
free_agents.outlook: Joshua Palmer will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he's to reprise his big-play, low-volume role in the Bills passing game in a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Palmer missed the team's Week 5 tilt with the Rams and has just three catches on the year. Averaging 26.7 yards per catch, Palmer has shown he can do more with less, but the lack of consistent targets in a run-first offense makes for a high-risk, medium-reward option.

free_agents.name: Noah Fant
free_agents.outlook: Noah Fant is expected to remain one of the Saints' top tight ends in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Fant was ineffective in his return from an abdomen injury during the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching his lone target for seven yards. Through four appearances this season, Fant is tied for the most receiving touchdowns (three) on the Saints and ranks fourth in receiving yards (73). He likely won't be fantasy relevant in the Week 6 unless finding the end zone, which is unlikely against a Giants defense that's allowed just two touchdowns to TEs this season.
